Subject: POC: Prompt set & eval plan — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps to kick off the POC evaluation: 

Summary of needs
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant that summarizes patient intake and suggests next steps for nurses.
- Success criteria (as discussed): median generation latency < 350ms at 8 concurrent users, top-1 accuracy match to current triage taxonomy >= 88% on labeled test set, and cost per 1k tokens under the threshold you provided.

Proposed POC plan (timeline + ownership)
- Week 1 (this week): Collection of prompt set and historical logs from Acme Health — action: Alex / Priya to upload anonymized prompts/log snippets and a small labeled set (approx 500 examples).
- Week 2: Redwood builds eval harness and runs baseline models + quantization configs.
- Week 3: Joint review of results, iterate prompts, and identify any quality regressions to tune.
- Week 4: Final run and handoff with performance dashboard + recommendations.

What we need from you now (priority)
1) Upload a sample prompt file (CSV) and a small anonymized logs archive (zip) — prefer: prompt, context, expected_label columns.
2) Confirm preferred evaluation metric (precision@1 vs. exact match) and the stakeholder who will approve success.
3) Finalize POC dates by EOD Friday so we can reserve dedicated run capacity.

Attachments: I attached a short eval plan (redwood_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf) with the proposed metrics and config notes.

If those deliverables look good I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) to own the eval harness and Vivek for capacity/throughput tuning.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the eval plan. A few quick items: 

- We can provide the prompt CSV and a small logs archive by COB Thursday. We will scrub PHI and provide synthetic IDs — file names: acme_prompt_samples_v1.csv and acme_logs_sample.zip.
- For metrics, clinical lead prefers exact match on triage category + a secondary metric of top-2 containment (since some intents are close). I think your precision@1 mapping to exact match is fine.
- Approver: Priya Shah (Head of Clinical Ops).

One question: are you able to run the baseline on a 2-quantized variant? We want to see both accuracy and cost tradeoffs.

Alex
Product Manager, Acme Health
